name: Nick Fuentes
role: American white-nationalist and Catholic-integralist streamer and commentator (host of America First, b. 1998)
summary: Fuentes advocates an America First nationalism centred on a predominantly white and Christian country, mass deportation, opposition to US support for Israel, and male authority in family and public life. He opposes women’s suffrage and supports a powerful executive; his economic proposals include protective tariffs, strategic industrial subsidies and public works.

notes: Later pass, 2026-11-08: reviewed every existing answer and every current statement, including candidates, against the Carlson and Morgan interviews and additional Neel interview. Automatic captions have no speaker labels, so retained answers from them are at most medium confidence and restricted to clear question-and-answer context. Checked the local reference-book filenames (no own book found), MediaSum (zero matching transcripts) and Lex Fridman (zero episodes); the local parliamentary corpora do not cover this commentator. Searched thin economy, ecology, technology, world, government and means themes, including healthcare, wages, taxation, climate, nuclear power, trade and alliances. Fight/Fudgie episode downloads returned 403; no further access to those episode pages attempted, and GitHub search found the Alex Jones mirror rather than the requested America First episodes. Secondary reports and jokes without a verified original were not converted into positions. Scholarly abstract s6 supplies context only; its critical characterisations do not establish answers. The Crowder interview supplies direct industrial-policy and gun-control positions. A retrieved 2022 oil clip mixes claims about infinite oil with an assertion that he is a scientist; without a clear sincere position it was not used to manufacture ecology answers. Moral neutrality of technology was not treated as political neutrality. No own book was found in the local reference library. Original automatic captions for the Neel interview were retrieved and checked against the third-party transcript; the third-party transcript is not cited as evidence. Final cross-check: the January 2024 violent-loyalty excerpt includes an immediate parody disclaimer, so it is not treated as a sincere contrary position or an action; uncertainty about sincerity keeps the nonviolence answer low. Reported July 2023 holy-war remarks led to a preserved video page without a readable transcript and a YouTube search with no relevant original result; those secondhand descriptions were not substituted for an inspected original. Arrests for obstruction were not treated as a general policy of suppressing political opposition. Final result: 59 to 49 known answers, 56 existing records changed, 102 candidate entries added; uncertainty passes.
